evals.prompt: Before we deploy our new Terraform stack in `ap-south-1` (Mumbai), calculate a pre-deployment monthly AWS cost breakdown using live `ap-south-1` pricing (`awspricing`): 3 NAT Gateways (processing 2 TB/month total), 2 `m7g.large` On-Demand Linux EC2 instances (730 hrs/mo each with 100 GB `gp3` EBS per instance), 1 Application Load Balancer (15 LCU-hours average), and a Single-AZ `db.r7g.large` RDS PostgreSQL instance with 200 GB `gp3` storage.
expectations: Activates the aws-finops-and-cost skill and queries `awspricing` MCP tools for `ap-south-1` (Asia Pacific Mumbai) unit rates with zero raw `aws` CLI shell commands
Produces a structured itemized monthly cost table separating fixed hourly baseline costs (`730 hours/month` math) from usage-driven data/LCU charges
Automatically flags high-impact IaC cost traps in the proposed architecture (such as 3 NAT Gateways without S3/DynamoDB Gateway Endpoints and On-Demand vs Savings Plans/Graviton opportunities)

evals.prompt: Review this proposed CDK/Terraform architecture for FinOps cost traps before `apply`: (1) 3 per-AZ NAT Gateways routing 15 TB/month of S3 and ECR image pulls from private EKS nodes, (2) 40 TB of `gp2` EBS volumes, (3) `m5.2xlarge` x86 stateless API workers and `db.r5.2xlarge` RDS PostgreSQL, and (4) CloudWatch Log Groups with no `retention_in_days` set.
expectations: Activates the aws-finops-and-cost skill

Flags all 4 major IaC cost traps: (1) adding free S3/DynamoDB Gateway VPC Endpoints + evaluating ECR Interface Endpoints vs `$0.045+/GB` NAT data processing, (2) migrating `gp2` -> `gp3` (~20% lower $/GB-month + decoupled 3,000 baseline IOPS / 125 MB/s), (3) modernizing `m5`/`r5` x86 to AWS Graviton (`m7g`/`m8g` and `db.r7g`/`db.r8g`) for ~20% better price-performance, and (4) setting explicit CloudWatch Logs `retention_in_days` + S3 Intelligent-Tiering/lifecycle policies

evals.prompt: We run 24 `c6i.4xlarge` On-Demand Linux instances 24x7 at 14% peak CPU and 22% memory utilization, plus a nightly 2-hour stateless batch video-transcoding fleet of 40 instances. Give us a deterministic FinOps optimization sequence (rightsizing + architecture + purchase model) and explain why buying Compute Savings Plans BEFORE rightsizing is a mistake.
expectations: Activates the aws-finops-and-cost skill

Mandates rightsizing and Graviton migration (`c7g`/`c8g`, stepping down instance sizes based on CPU + memory p95/max metrics) BEFORE purchasing 1-year/3-year Compute or EC2 Instance Savings Plans so you do not over-commit hourly $/hr spend
Recommends EC2 Spot Instances (diversified instance pools / Karpenter or ASG capacity-optimized) for the fault-tolerant stateless 2-hour nightly batch fleet

evals.prompt: Our Aurora PostgreSQL Provisioned cluster (`2 x db.r7g.2xlarge` in `us-east-1`, 4 TB storage) currently spends $1,150/month on compute, $400/month on storage, and $950/month on `VolumeReadIOPs`/`VolumeWriteIOPs` ($2,500/month total). Analyze whether switching to `aurora-iopt1` (Aurora I/O-Optimized) saves money using deterministic break-even math, and check whether non-prod clones should use Serverless v2 scale-to-zero.
expectations: Activates the aws-finops-and-cost skill

Applies the ~25% I/O-spend break-even rule explicitly (`$950 / $2,500 = 38%` of total Aurora spend on I/O, or explicitly computes `+30%` compute + `+125%` storage vs `$0` I/O = `~$1,495 + $900 = $2,395/mo` vs `$2,500/mo`) to show `aurora-iopt1` saves money and eliminates I/O spike variance
Recommends Aurora Serverless v2 with `MinCapacity = 0` (scale-to-zero) or automated stop/start schedules for idle non-production dev/QA clusters

evals.prompt: Audit our block storage plan: 50 `gp2` volumes of 500 GB each (`25 TB` total) where workloads only need 3,000 IOPS and 125 MB/s throughput, plus 18 unattached `available` EBS volumes and 400 orphaned EBS snapshots older than 18 months. Quantify the `gp2` -> `gp3` savings formula and safe cleanup guardrails.
expectations: Activates the aws-finops-and-cost skill

Demonstrates the deterministic `gp2` (`~$0.10/GB-mo`) vs `gp3` (`~$0.08/GB-mo` in `us-east-1` baseline, ~20% storage savings with 3,000 IOPS and 125 MB/s included free) calculation across `25,000 GB` (`~$500/month` / `~$6,000/year` savings via online zero-downtime `ModifyVolume`)
Outlines safe governance for unattached `available` volumes and aged snapshots (checking `LastAttachTime`/tags, taking a final snapshot or archiving via Data Lifecycle Manager before deleting)

evals.prompt: How do we embed shift-left FinOps cost visibility directly into GitHub Actions pull requests for Terraform / OpenTofu so engineers see exact monthly cost deltas (`+$420/mo`) and FinOps guardrails fail PRs that exceed budget thresholds?
expectations: Activates the aws-finops-and-cost skill
Details wiring `infracost breakdown` / `infracost diff` in PR CI against Terraform HCL/plan JSON with a baseline comparison against `main`

evals.prompt: Our AWS bill jumped by $4,800/month under `EC2-Other` (`DataTransfer-Regional-Bytes`) and `AmazonS3` (`TimedStorage-ByteHrs` + incomplete multipart uploads) even though instance counts stayed flat. Explain the architectural root causes and IaC fixes for both.
expectations: Activates the aws-finops-and-cost skill

Explains `DataTransfer-Regional-Bytes` (`$0.01/GB` each direction = `$0.02/GB` round-trip across Availability Zones from chatty cross-AZ pods/microservices, Kafka/MSK consumers, or ALB/NLB cross-zone traffic) and recommends AZ-aware routing / topology hints
Fixes S3 storage bloat via S3 Intelligent-Tiering / `glacier` lifecycle transitions and mandatory `abort_incomplete_multipart_upload_days` (e.g., 7 days) on every S3 bucket in IaC

evals.prompt: We have 12 ephemeral developer/staging environments, each spinning up a 3-AZ VPC with 3 NAT Gateways (`36 NAT Gateways` total costing ~$1,200/month sitting completely idle!). Compare safe FinOps patterns for non-production vs production NAT topologies in IaC.
expectations: Activates the aws-finops-and-cost skill

Distinguishes production (2-3 AZ NAT Gateways + free S3/DynamoDB Gateway Endpoints for AZ fault isolation) from non-production dev/ephemeral stacks (1 single shared NAT Gateway, centralized Transit Gateway egress VPC, IPv6 egress-only internet gateway where supported, or `fck-nat` / NAT instance)
Shows the exact hourly fixed cost impact (`36 * 730 * ~$0.045/hr` saved down to 1 NAT per dev VPC or shared egress)

evals.prompt: Use `awspricing` or `awsknowledge` to compare Amazon DynamoDB On-Demand (`PAY_PER_REQUEST`) vs Provisioned Capacity (`PROVISIONED` with Application Auto Scaling + Reserved Capacity) after AWS's Nov 2024 50% On-Demand price reduction, and give clear rules for which billing mode to put in IaC.
